body: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md:18 says an entry applies when its projectPath equals this project's root or its scope is user, and the entry for this project wins over the user entry; :20 and :32 take the applying ok@ and ok-conduct@ entries by that rule. The skill reads neither the 'enabled' field nor the 'projectEnabled' field. 'claude plugin list --json' on this machine today prints both fields on every entry (for example ok-conduct@ok-plugins: scope user, enabled true, projectEnabled false), so the filed Problem holds and understates: a per-project enablement field exists too, and the skill ignores it. Mechanism: the list prints one entry per install, at user and project scope, enabled or not. A disabled install is not loaded, so the 'installed' line can name a version no session here loads, beside a 'governing' line read from the session itself. Corpus: story see-governing-versions owes 'which plugin version actually governs my current session or project, alongside what is installed'; it is silent on which install counts when several apply, on scope precedence, and on enabled state. Decision vendored-skills says 'The plugin system delivers only the user-scoped plugins', so a project-scoped install of ok or ok-conduct lies outside the designed shape; the corpus says nothing on it. Harm: until the story says what 'installed' names, no accept-list entry covers the choice; once it does, a line that names a different install is A9 (a version line that is not so, which the user acts on). Options: (a) 'installed' names the install that would govern a new session here: the project's entry over the user's, and only an enabled one (decide whether projectEnabled counts too). Cost: a story clause and a skill edit; a disabled-only install reports unknown, so a user cannot see a copy that sits on disk. (b) 'installed' names any install present for this project or user, enabled or not, the project's first. Cost: the story clause only, the skill already does this; the line can name a version nothing loads, which weakens the drift signal the story exists for. (c), which the filer missed: report every applying install with its scope and enabled state. Cost: the skill's fixed five-line report (SKILL.md step 6) grows to a list, and the story's single 'what is installed' becomes several. Rule with sibling version-surface-absent-outside-integrated-projects, which bears on the same story.

Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok-conduct/hooks/session-start:9 injects into every session 'If the ok-conduct output style is active, its delivery rules govern this session; /ok-version reports the conduct actually governing.' The skill ships only at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md, and the converge core materializes it (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:124, :129) only into a project that integrates ok-planner. plugins/ok/skills holds only 'ok'; plugins/ok-conduct holds CLAUDE.md, hooks, and output-styles, no skill. plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md:45 accepts a declined bootstrap and records 'not integrated (declined)'. plugins/ok-conduct/CLAUDE.md:16 says the hook and /ok-version both read the conduct stamp. The filed Problem holds. Mechanism: the conduct is user-scoped and loads in every project; the version skill is vendored and exists only where ok-planner is integrated, so outside such a project the hook names a command the user cannot run, and no surface shows the governing conduct beside the installed one. /ok reports carried and vendored suite versions (plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md:106) but not the governing conduct, and it updates plugins first (:20-26), so it is no read-only version check. Corpus: story see-governing-versions owes 'a suite consumer' the governing version 'alongside what is installed', silent on whether a conduct-only user is a suite consumer; concept conduct: the conduct governs 'in every project and session the user runs' and is 'outside any project's vendored presence'; decision vendored-skills: 'The plugin system delivers only the user-scoped plugins — the front door carrying the family, the conduct, and the web setup skills', the machine-shared layer is 'the administrator, the conduct, and the web setup skills', and 'no skill depends on it being active'. Harm: A9, as the merge agent confirmed: the hook tells the session a command reports the governing conduct where that command does not exist. Options: (a) the story owes the view in every project, so a version surface ships in a user-scoped plugin (the front door or ok-conduct). Cost: vendored-skills' machine-shared layer widens by a skill and the decision must say so; one idiom per job then forces the vendored /ok-version to be retired or reduced, and a user-scoped skill reads the project's vendored stamp only where one exists. (b) the story owes the view only in a project that integrates ok-planner, and the hook names /ok-version only where it exists (for example, when the project holds the vendored skill). Cost: a conduct-only user has no surface for the governing conduct; the story narrows. (c), which the filer missed: the hook names no command and states only the installed conduct version, and the story narrows as in (b). Cost: an integrated project loses the pointer to /ok-version too. (d), which the filer missed: /ok's report carries the governing and installed conduct versions. Cost: /ok updates plugins before it reports, so its 'installed' value is the post-update one, and a version check becomes an administration act. Rule with sibling installed-version-entry-selection, which bears on the same story.

Harm: none observed; a backout agent reads its own exception; the risk is a reader of the shared rule or SKILL.md:154 (the orchestrator, a verifier) treating a backout's restore of a left-alone file as a breach.
